title: Workspace watcher publishes every file and directory of a new Git-ignored worktree tree to the session's 'Workspace changes during turn' panel
outcome: Creating a large, Git-ignored tree inside a watched root (for example a new `.worktrees/<name>` checkout) does not publish an entry per file and directory to a session's 'Workspace changes during turn' panel. Ignored paths are filtered at the source, without enumerating the tree and without a new costly scan. Real changes to tracked or untracked, non-ignored files in the session's own worktree stay visible.
acceptance: Through production watcher/attribution/publication, a Git-ignored subtree created inside a watched repository (including .worktrees/<name>) does not produce per-file or per-directory changes in the ancestor session turn summary or UI event stream.

Tracked and non-ignored untracked changes in the session own worktree remain visible; an independently active nested worktree under a parent-ignored directory retains its own real changes, without attributing the whole new checkout to the ancestor session.

The filter runs before excess turn-summary/UI materialization, without recursive tree enumeration, a Git subprocess per event, or new costly monitoring; check-credit ordering and conservative coverage are preserved. Large change sets are coalesced before transport and the UI into bounded summaries with counts and a small path sample, instead of one entry per file, while covering invalidations preserve meaningful own-worktree refreshes.

Behavioural regression tests exercise ignored-subtree suppression and positive own/nested-worktree cases through the production path, first demonstrate RED on the pre-fix code, then pass with the fix; required focused checks, independent review pair and exact-input FULL pass under standing rules.
